definitions.gloss: lingering regret; reluctance to part; something left unresolved in one's heart
definitions.explanation: A feeling of regret about something left undone, or reluctance to leave a place or person. Often used when parting ways or reflecting on missed opportunities.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つだけ{心残|こころのこ}りなのは、{祖父|そふ}に{会|あ}えなかったことだ。
examples.english: My one regret is that I couldn't see my grandfather.

examples.japanese: もっと{色々|いろいろ}な{場所|ばしょ}を{回|まわ}りたかったが、{時間|じかん}が{足|た}りず{心残|こころのこ}りだった。
examples.english: I wanted to visit more places, but I didn't have enough time — it was a lingering regret.

notes:
Describes a gentle, wistful feeling of regret — not sharp guilt, but a sense that something was left unfinished or that one wishes things had gone differently. Often used when leaving a place or at the end of an experience.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心残|こころのこ}りがある: to have a lingering regret
- {心残|こころのこ}りはない: to have no regrets
- {心残|こころのこ}りなく: without regret, with no loose ends
- {唯一|ゆいいつ}の{心残|こころのこ}り: one's only regret

USAGE:
Also used as a na-adjective: {心残|こころのこ}りな{気持|きも}ち (a feeling of lingering regret). The phrase {心残|こころのこ}りなく is often used positively: to be able to do something without any regrets.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後悔|こうかい}: regret — stronger, implies wishing one had acted differently
- {未練|みれん}: lingering attachment — stronger emotional pull, often about relationships
- {名残|なごり}{惜|お}しい: reluctant to part — specifically about parting from a person or place
